title: Training-Free Linear Routing for Sparse Attention via Attention-Mass Prediction

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution aims to show that aligning query-key distributions geometrically is the wrong objective for training-free sparse-attention routing. None of the prior papers explicitly establish or report this empirical relationship. While some papers (e.g., [5], [22], [13]) discuss sparse attention methods and their trade-offs, none directly address the geometric alignment of query-key distributions as a flawed objective for training-free sparse-attention routing. This specific empirical finding is not covered.

### Mechanism
The contribution applies geometric moment matching via gauge-coupled whitening to align query and key distributions before symmetric k-means routing. Paper [11] ("Geometric Moment Alignment for Domain Adaptation via Siegel Embeddings") uses geometric moment matching to align distributions, albeit in the context of domain adaptation rather than sparse attention. The underlying primitive of geometric moment matching is equivalent across domains, making the mechanism covered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation compares attention-mass recall (50.7% vs 51.3%) using symmetric k-means routing on Qwen2.5-7B. Paper [5] ("The Sparse Frontier") conducts large-scale empirical evaluations of training-free sparse attention methods, including symmetric k-means routing, across multiple models, tasks, and sparsity levels. The evaluation design (comparing sparse attention methods using attention-mass recall or similar metrics) is substantively equivalent, even though the specific benchmark and model differ. Thus, the evaluation is covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of sparse attention routing for long-context LLM inference. Papers [5], [22], and [13] all address sparse attention methods for long-context LLMs, which is the same general application area. While the specific sub-problem or model instance may differ, the domain is covered.
